ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
An object with mass $m=2\mathrm{kg}$ is subjected to a horizontal pulling force $F$ and starts from rest to undergo uniformly accelerated linear motion on a smooth horizontal surface. After a time $t=6\mathrm{s}$, the displacement is $x=54\mathrm{m}$.

1. The magnitude of the average velocity $v$ of the object during this time period
2. The magnitude of the acceleration of the object $a$
3. The magnitude of the horizontal pulling force $F$.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: An object with mass $m=2\mathrm{kg}$ is subjected to a horizontal pulling force $F$ and starts from rest to undergo uniformly accelerated linear motion on a smooth horizontal surface. After a time $t=6\mathrm{s}$, the displacement is $x=54\mathrm{m}$. 1. The magnitude of the average velocity $v$ of the object during this time period 2. The magnitude of the acceleration of the object $a$ 3. The magnitude of the horizontal pulling force $F$.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Given m=2 kg, t=6 s, displacement x=54 m, initial velocity u=0, uniformly accelerated motion, and a smooth horizontal surface. First compute the average velocity over the interval: v_avg = x/t = 54/6 = 9 m/s. Since the object starts from rest, use x = (1/2) a t^2, so a = 2x/t^2 = 2×54/6^2 = 108/36 = 3 m/s^2. On a smooth horizontal surface, the horizontal pulling force is the net horizontal force, so by Newton's second law F = ma = 2×3 = 6 N.
